interpretation: Corridor orientations are strongly non-uniform (E/SE dominant, 85/108 ≈ 79%), which is typical for Mediterranean megalithic corridors facing the rising sun.  The corridor circular mean (117°) is closer to the December solstice sunrise (124°) than the June solstice (79°), but this is also consistent with a generic SE bias — astronomical intent is underdetermined.  The uniform-random control confirms the orientation structure is real (z vs uniform = 17.8), but the interpretation as intentional astronomical alignment requires independent evidence.  Spatial NND is lower than uniform-rectangle expectation (z < -10), but this is expected for a river-valley survey — the rectangular bbox null includes areas of unsuitable terrain.  Verdict: ORIENTATION_STRUCTURE, astronomical alignment UNDERDETERMINED.
caveat: Corridor orientation is only measurable for ~108/151 tombs (those with preserved corridors).  Solar azimuths computed for epoch -3000 with ±1° ephemeris precision; precession over the megalithic period (~4000–2000 BCE) shifts solstice azimuth by <1°.  The 'alignment' comparison is illustrative, not a claim.
